claims.quote: Five such coaches were filled as I watched, and were shot up the guides to be locked on to their waiting packets three hundred feet nearer the stars.
claims.description: Mail is loaded into large coaches that are hoisted up towers and locked onto airships floating hundreds of feet up.

claims.quote: Blessed be Sargent, Ahrens, and the Dubois brothers, who invented the cloud-breakers of the world whereby we travel in security!
claims.description: Beacons that pierce cloud layers let airships navigate safely through cloud and fog.

claims.quote: Raise a few feet of that all but invisible plate three-eighths of an inch and she will yaw five miles to port or starboard ere she is under control again.
claims.description: A nearly invisible hinged rudder plate controls the steering of a large airship.

claims.quote: Fleury's gas can lift anything, as the world-famous trials of '89 showed
claims.description: A lifting gas can carry almost any load, though its expansion requires very large tanks.

claims.quote: Even Fleury who begat it and, unlike Magniac, died a multi-millionaire, could not explain how the restless little imp shuddering in the U-tube can, in the fractional fraction of a second, strike the furious blast of gas into a chill greyish-green liquid
claims.description: A vacuum-tube effect condenses a high-speed gas stream into liquid in an instant, forming a closed cycle that drives the airship's engines.

claims.quote: Our General Communication dial has caught her talk and begins to eavesdrop.
claims.description: Airships carry a radio-like dial that picks up and relays transmissions from other aircraft.

claims.quote: Her underbody colloid is open land her transporter-slings hang down like tentacles.
claims.description: Airships lower cables with cradles beneath them to lift people and cargo from another airship in mid-air.
